title: KMS/HSM Terraform gateway: idempotent secrets reconciliation and health probes for VPC installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Private (VPC) customers run a mix of cloud KMS (AWS/GCP) and on-prem HSMs. Existing terraform modules provide provisioning but we lack a single, idempotent gateway module that ensures secrets written to multiple backends remain reconciled, supports controlled rotation, and exposes deterministic health checks for automation.

Objective: Deliver a reusable Terraform module (redwood_kms_hsm_gateway) and companion reconciliation job that: (1) provisions KMS/HSM connectors and Secrets Manager/Vault bindings, (2) performs idempotent dual-write with tombstone markers for safe migrations, (3) exposes a standardized health probe and canary-decrypt probe for operator automation, and (4) includes drift detection and self-heal hooks for private deployments. Module must work across AWS/GCP and on-prem PKCS#11 HSMs via a lightweight agent or sidecar.

Why this matters: Several enterprise customers experienced failed rotations or asymmetric writes during private upgrades. A single verified module reduces configuration drift, speeds upgrades, and lowers support load by surfacing deterministic health signals to Console and the private control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module redwood_kms_hsm_gateway published under github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules with README and examples for AWS-KMS + Vault, GCP-KMS + Secrets Manager, and PKCS11 HSM + Vault
Module supports idempotent dual-write mode with optional tombstone marker semantics to safely reconcile diverged secrets
Expose terraform outputs that wire up: health_probe_url, canary_secret_path, rotation_status_log_s3 (or equivalent), and reconciliation_job_id
Health probe returns structured JSON (status, last_success_ts, last_decrypt_ok, active_key_version) and is documented in Console observability contracts
Automated reconciliation Terraform null_resource (or lambda) that can be scheduled and produces a reconciliation report artifact in S3/GCS/Drive
Canary decryption test succeeds after module deploy and is included in acceptance pipeline; failure triggers automatic rollback when configured
Module includes integration tests and unit tests (terraform-compliance + terratest) that run in CI and pass for at least AWS and a mocked PKCS11 HSM
design_notes: Core module shape: provider-agnostic interface with implementation plugins. API surface: providers = ["aws_kms", "gcp_kms", "pkcs11_hsm"], secrets_backends = ["vault", "secrets_manager"]

Dual-write model: primary_write -> tombstone_marker -> secondary_write. Reconciliation compares tombstone versions and writes reconciliation result as audit marker to secrets_reconciler/registry/<secret>.
Health probe contract: GET /_health returns {"status": "ok|degraded|failed", "last_decrypt_ok": ISO8601, "key_versions": [string], "drift_detected": boolean}

PKCS11 HSM integration: provide helper module that deploys a minimal sidecar agent (docker) that exposes a gRPC wrap to the HSM; terraform config wires the agent as a managed service in the VPC and creates network policy rules

Security: all sensitive outputs suppressed by default; module requires kms_key_arn or hsm_slot_identifier but never prints key material. Vault auth uses approle with short-lived tokens rotated by the reconciler
Rollback behavior: if canary_decrypt fails, module leaves previous mapping intact and emits structured failure to ops channel (Slack/GCP PubSub)
implementation_steps: 1) Prototype module interface and examples for AWS-KMS + Vault (2 days)
2) Implement dual-write tombstone logic in module with optional null_resource runner for reconciliation (3 days)
3) Add PKCS11 helper submodule and sidecar agent container spec (4 days)
4) Implement health probe endpoint and Terraform outputs wiring (2 days)
5) Build terratest suite and CI job that spins a lightweight HSM mock and AWS sandbox (3 days)
6) Security review, threat modeling, and docs update (2 days)
7) Internal beta: deploy to two private customers with engineer-on-call and run reconciliation for 2 weeks (7 days)
8) Iterate on issues found during beta and finalize module for release (3 days)
test_plan: Integration: terratest runs against AWS sandbox using a real KMS key and Vault test instance
HSM mock test: use softHSM instance in CI to validate PKCS11 flows
Canary scenario: deploy module, rotate key version, verify canary_decrypt passes and secrets remain accessible
Failure scenario: simulate network partition between reconcilier and secondary backend and assert tombstone markers prevent data loss
Chaos: randomized order of writes and reboots of sidecar agent to ensure reconciliation converges
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Module merged to repo and published as pre-release; internal infra teams to try on staging VPC
Stage 2: Invite two private customers for opt-in beta with assigned SEs; enable verbose logs and 30-day retention for reconciliation reports
Stage 3: After 2-week beta and sign-off, publish stable module and announce in Console release notes and partner channels
Stage 4: Offer migration guide and a one-click reconcilier runbook in Console; default policy for new private deployments to use gateway module
monitoring: Expose logs to central telemetry with structured events: reconcile_report_id, affected_secrets_count, successful_writes, failed_writes
Health probe scraped by Prometheus using the /_metrics bridge; incidents route to on-call via PagerDuty if last_decrypt_ok older than 15m
Create a Console dashboard tile that shows recent reconciliation runs, failure rates, and per-customer drift status
